# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 16 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 16 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_016_page_001.jpg

---

1 For these reasons they were fittingly punished by means of like creatures and tormented by a swarm of vermin.

2 Instead of this punishment you treated your people kindly, and to satisfy their craving you prepared a delicacy to delight the palate, providing quails for their appetite.

3 So that those, desiring food, might turn away from necessary appetite on account of the loathsome creatures sent among them; while these, after a brief period of want, might partake of extraordinary fare.

4 For it was necessary that inescapable destitution should overtake those who were exercising tyranny; but to these it was merely shown how their enemies were being tormented.

5 For when the fierce wrath of wild beasts came upon them and they were being destroyed by the bites of writhing serpents, your anger did not persist to the end.

6 But as a chastening warning they were troubled for a short time, having a token of salvation to remind them of the commandment of your law;

7 for the one who turned toward it was saved, not by what he saw, but by you, the Savior of all.

8 And by this also you convinced our enemies that you are the one who rescues from every evil.

9 For them, bites of locusts and flies brought death, and no remedy was found for their life, because they were worthy to be punished by such things.

10 But your sons were not overcome even by the fangs of venomous serpents; for your mercy came to their aid and healed them.

11 For they were stung to remind them of your words, and were quickly delivered, lest sinking into deep forgetfulness they should become unable to make use of your loving-kindness.

12 For neither herb nor poultice healed them, but your word, O Lord, which heals all things.

13 For you have power over life and death, and you lead down to the gates of Hades and lead back up again.

14 A man may kill through his wickedness, but when the spirit has departed it does not return, nor does he bring back the soul that has been taken.

15 But it is not possible to escape your hand.

16 For the ungodly who refused to acknowledge you were scourged by the might of your arm, pursued by extraordinary rains and hailstorms and relentless downpours, and utterly consumed by fire.

17 For — most marvelous of all — in water, which quenches everything, fire burned more fiercely; for the world champions the cause of the righteous.

18 At one time the flame was restrained so as not to consume the creatures sent against the ungodly, so that they, seeing this, might know that they were being pursued by the judgment of God;

19 and at another time even in the midst of water it burned beyond the power of fire, that it might destroy the crops of an unrighteous land.

20 In their place you fed your people with food of angels, and without their toil you supplied from heaven bread ready-made, possessing every delight and suited to every taste.

21 For your provision showed forth your sweetness toward your children, and serving the wish of the one who received it, it was transformed into what each one desired.

22 But snow and ice withstood fire without melting, so that they might know that fire was destroying the crops of the enemies, blazing in the hailstones and flashing in the rainstorms.

23 But again fire forgot its own power, so that the righteous might be nourished.

24 For creation, serving you its Maker, exerts itself for punishment against the unrighteous, and relaxes for blessing on behalf of those who trust in you.

25 Therefore at that time too, taking on all forms, it was obedient to your all-nourishing grace, according to the desire of those who had need,

26 so that your children whom you love, O Lord, might learn that it is not the various crops that nourish man, but that your word preserves those who trust in you.

27 For what the fire had not destroyed melted away when merely warmed by a fleeting ray of sun,

28 so that it might be known that one must rise before the sun to give you thanks and approach you at the dawning of the light.

29 For the hope of the ungrateful will melt like wintry ice and flow away like water without use.
